titleEn: The SS United States has been deliberately sunk – this is how marine life will colonise the world’s largest artificial reef
titleZh: 美国号邮轮被沉入海底后，海洋生物将如何占据这座人工礁？
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: As a marine ecologist and keen scuba diver, I’ve long been fascinated by what happens when a large structure is introduced to the sea. Within hours, microscopic organisms begin colonising its surfaces, forming a thin biological layer. Over the following months and years, barnacles, mussels, sponges and other marine life become established, creating a new habitat that attracts fish and a diverse range of species.
paragraphs.zh: 作为一名海洋生态学家和潜水爱好者，我一直着迷于当一个大型结构被引入大海时会发生什么。几个小时内，微生物开始在其表面定居，形成一层薄薄的生物层。在接下来的几个月和几年里，藤壶，贻贝，海绵和其他海洋生物开始定居，创造了一个新的栖息地，吸引了鱼类和各种物种。

paragraphs.en: This week, one of the world’s most famous ocean liners, the SS United States, was sunk off the coast of Florida. At 302 metres long, it has become the world’s largest artificial reef. It is a very exciting prospect to one day dive on such a giant, and to see how it changes as marine life makes it home.
paragraphs.zh: 本周，世界上最著名的远洋客轮之一"美国号“在佛罗里达海岸附近沉没。长达302米的”美国号“已成为世界上最大的人工鱼礁。有一天，能在这样一个庞然大物上潜水，看看海洋生物在这里安家后会发生什么变化，真是令人兴奋的前景。

paragraphs.en: The SS United States was built as a luxury ocean liner, and its maiden voyage in 1952 captured the coveted Blue Riband by crossing the Atlantic in only three days and ten hours – a passenger liner record that remains unbroken.
paragraphs.zh: SS United States是作为一艘豪华远洋客轮建造的，1952年的处女航仅用了3天10小时就横渡了大西洋，获得了令人垂涎的蓝丝带-这是一个至今未被打破的客轮纪录。

paragraphs.en: As the years went by, commercial jetliners superseded transatlantic sea travel, and the vessel was retired and neglected for decades. Rather than facing the ignominy of a breaker’s yard, the legendary ship was bought by Okaloosa County, Florida, to turn it into a diving attraction.
paragraphs.zh: 随着时间的推移，商业喷气式客机取代了跨大西洋的海上旅行，这艘船退役并被忽视了几十年。这艘传奇的船没有面临破碎机码头的耻辱，而是被佛罗里达的奥卡卢萨县买下，把它变成了一个潜水景点。

paragraphs.en: The SS United States is a particularly enormous structure to introduce to the seabed – longer even than the Titanic. It will rest in around 55 metres of water, with its upper sections rising to within about 17 metres of the surface. This will create habitats at different depths, making it an unusually varied site for both wildlife and divers of different abilities.
paragraphs.zh: 美国号是一个特别巨大的结构，甚至比泰坦尼克号还要长。它将停留在大约55米的水下，其上部上升到水面17米以内。这将在不同的深度创造栖息地，使其成为野生动物和不同能力的潜水员的一个异常多样化的地方。

paragraphs.en: It will also eclipse the nearby 275-metre aircraft carrier USS Oriskany, deliberately sunk in 2006, to become the largest artificial reef on Earth.
paragraphs.zh: 它还将使附近275米长的航空母舰USS Oriskany黯然失色，该航母于2006年被故意击沉，成为地球上最大的人工礁。

paragraphs.en: So what do we expect to happen? Here’s a suggested ecological succession pattern, month-by-month.
paragraphs.zh: 那么我们期望发生什么呢？这是一个建议的生态演替模式，逐月。

paragraphs.en: First, microorganisms arrive
paragraphs.zh: 首先，微生物到达

paragraphs.en: The first organisms to colonise the SS United States will be almost invisible. Within hours of immersion, marine bacteria and microalgae will begin attaching themselves to its cleaned metal surfaces, forming a thin layer of “biofilm”.
paragraphs.zh: 第一批在“美国号”上定居的生物几乎是看不见的。在浸泡的几个小时内，海洋细菌和微藻将开始附着在其清洁的金属表面，形成一层薄薄的“生物膜”。

paragraphs.en: This slime is the foundation of the new ecosystem. As the biofilm develops, it releases chemical cues that help drifting larvae recognise the surface as a suitable place to settle. Carried by Gulf currents, these tiny organisms begin attaching themselves to the structure. By the end of the first three months, a variety of small animals and algae will have established themselves on the hull, beginning the transformation of bare metal into a living reef.
paragraphs.zh: 这种粘液是新生态系统的基础。随着生物膜的发展，它释放出化学信号，帮助漂流的幼虫识别出表面是一个适合定居的地方。在海湾洋流的推动下，这些微小的生物开始附着在结构上。到前三个月结束时，各种小动物和藻类将在船体上定居，开始将裸露的金属转变为活的珊瑚礁。

paragraphs.en: Then the ship becomes covered in marine life
paragraphs.zh: 然后船就被海洋生物覆盖了

paragraphs.en: As the biofilm matures, larger organisms arrive to feed on it. These include more mobile invertebrates like sea urchins and porcelain crabs, and filter-feeders like oysters and mussels which attach themselves to vertical walls where the currents tend to send the most nutrients their way.
paragraphs.zh: 随着生物膜的成熟，更大的生物体来到这里以其为食，其中包括更多的移动的无脊椎动物，如海胆和瓷蟹，以及滤食性动物，如牡蛎和贻贝，它们附着在垂直的墙壁上，水流倾向于将最多的营养物质送到它们的地方。

paragraphs.en: Fish and larger predators move in
paragraphs.zh: 鱼类和大型捕食者进入

paragraphs.en: By the end of the first year, hard corals will begin to establish themselves permanently. The transformation will still be in its early stages, but over the next five to ten years the hull will become increasingly encrusted with corals, sponges and other marine life. At some point, casual divers will no longer see a ship covered in coral, but a coral-covered reef that happens to contain a ship.
paragraphs.zh: 到第一年年底，硬珊瑚将开始永久地定居下来。这种转变仍处于早期阶段，但在接下来的五到十年里，船体将越来越多地被珊瑚、海绵和其他海洋生物所覆盖。在某个时候，偶尔潜水的人将不再看到一艘被珊瑚覆盖的船，而是一个珊瑚覆盖的礁石，碰巧包含一艘船。

paragraphs.en: As the reef develops, fish will be attracted by the shelter and the growing supply of food. Smaller fish will begin to find refuge to evade open-water predators.
paragraphs.zh: 随着珊瑚礁的发展，鱼类会被庇护所和不断增加的食物所吸引。较小的鱼类将开始寻找避难所，以躲避开放水域的捕食者。

paragraphs.en: Snappers and groupers are among the medium-sized reef fish that will begin to take up permanent residency around the wreck, using the long internal corridors for protection. Larger predators, including barracuda, king mackerel and sharks, could also patrol its decks and upper sections.
paragraphs.zh: 笛鲷和石斑鱼等中等大小的珊瑚鱼将开始在沉船周围永久居住，利用长长的内部走廊进行保护。梭鱼、鲭鱼王和鲨鱼等更大的食肉动物也可能在甲板和上层巡逻。

paragraphs.en: The ship’s enormous size and varied structure will offer a range of habitats, from sheltered spaces for smaller fish to exposed areas where larger, free-swimming species can hunt. Over time, these interactions could create a complex food web, turning the wreck into a significant biological hotspot.
paragraphs.zh: 这艘船的巨大尺寸和多样的结构将提供一系列栖息地，从较小鱼类的庇护空间到较大的自由游泳物种可以捕食的暴露区域。随着时间的推移，这些相互作用可能会形成一个复杂的食物网，将沉船变成一个重要的生物热点。

paragraphs.en: A common misconception is that artificial reefs simply concentrate fish that were already present, leaving surrounding waters poorer. In reality, while some fish are attracted from elsewhere, a large reef structure also creates vast amounts of new habitat and food.
paragraphs.zh: 一个常见的误解是，人工鱼礁只是集中了已经存在的鱼类，使周围的沃茨变差。实际上，虽然一些鱼类是从其他地方吸引来的，但大型珊瑚礁结构也创造了大量新的栖息地和食物。

paragraphs.en: As corals, sponges, barnacles and other reef builders colonise the wreck, they create food and shelter that did not previously exist, allowing the ecosystem to support more life overall. The result is generally not an underwater crowd gathered around a ship, but a gradual increase in the total amount of marine life the area can support.
paragraphs.zh: 随着珊瑚、海绵、藤壶和其他造礁生物在沉船上定居，它们创造了以前不存在的食物和庇护所，使生态系统能够支持更多的生命。结果通常不是水下人群聚集在一艘船周围，而是该地区可以支持的海洋生物总量逐渐增加。

paragraphs.en: Another widespread misconception is that marine scientists “seed” artificial reefs with organisms or their larvae. In reality, colonisation happens naturally: the Gulf of Mexico already harbours an abundant pool of drifting larvae and migratory fish. Artificially introducing marine life is unnecessary and risks introducing non-native species or pathogens.
paragraphs.zh: 另一个普遍存在的误解是，海洋科学家在人工礁上“播种”生物或其幼虫。实际上，殖民化是自然发生的：墨西哥湾已经有大量漂流幼虫和洄游鱼类。引入海洋生物是不必要的，而且有引入非本地物种或病原体的风险。

paragraphs.en: Instead, human engineering is largely about preparing the ship for sinking. This includes removing hazards such as oil, asbestos and loose wires, and sealing off parts of the vessel to prevent divers getting disorientated or lost in silt-outs deep in the hull.
paragraphs.zh: 相反，人体工程学主要是为船只的沉没做准备，包括清除油污、石棉和松动的电线等危险物质，以及密封船只的某些部分，以防止潜水员迷失方向或迷失在船体深处的淤泥中。

paragraphs.en: The scuttling of the SS United States represents a rare convergence of maritime history, ecology, and engineering. Transformed into the world’s largest artificial reef, this record-breaking ocean liner could potentially anchor a vibrant marine ecosystem for decades to come. I’m looking forward to seeing how that transformation unfolds – and maybe, one day, exploring it myself.
paragraphs.zh: “美国号”的沉没代表了海洋历史、生态学和工程学的罕见融合。这艘破纪录的远洋客轮被改造成世界上最大的人工鱼礁，可能会在未来几十年里锚住一个充满活力的海洋生态系统。我期待着看到这种转变是如何展开的--也许有一天，我自己也会探索它。
